RFC5882-10.2-1.note: Judge 2026-10-11 (independent re-judge after ef70c19e79 changed TestRFC5882AuthJoinDifferentAuthRefused; judge authored none of it). Row quotes Section 10.2 verbatim (rfc5882.txt 'BFD authentication SHOULD be used and is strongly encouraged.'). Ze's part: let an EBGP-advised BFD session run authenticated, hold it to that, and name the unauthenticated case. Unchanged units re-read against the 2026-09-30 judgement: + SignsItsSession (A bit, Auth Type 4, Len 28, Key ID 7, Up), - MismatchedNeighbor and - UnauthenticatedNeighbor (never Up, no fallback), - WithoutAuthRunsUnauthenticated; reactor + NamesAuthenticatedProfile and the four commit Warn units. Changed unit - AuthJoinDifferentAuthRefused now runs seven cases on both join arms (exact key, shared join): auth->none, none->auth, key id, secret, Auth Type alone (keyed-md5 vs keyed-sha1), keyed-sha1 then meticulous-keyed-sha1, and the Meticulous flag alone (resolved 'secure' auth with Meticulous inverted, sent under no profile because authTypeFromEnum ties each meticulous enum to its own wire Auth Type). Each asserts errors.Is ErrAuthMismatch, peer named, one session, first session's next Control packet keeps its auth or none. The earlier caveat (Type and Meticulous comparisons in engine sameAuth unexercised) is closed: judge re-ran go test -overlay with each comparison deleted; the Type mutant reddens only different_auth_type on both arms, the Meticulous mutant only different_meticulous_flag on both arms; clean run green (-race). Discrimination record for the negative (revert of joinAuthCheck) re-written at unit-sha 15bc152837a4dfa6; it proves the refusal path, the overlay mutants prove the field comparisons. + AuthJoinIdenticalAuthShares unchanged (same auth under two names; none twice). Remaining limit: the Meticulous-alone case is a request no profile can produce, so it guards the comparison rather than a configured path.

RFC5882-4.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor). SHIFTED by 6e063fb498 (tests: give ten assert-nothing tests a real assertion), whose hunks sit in untagged sibling tests and the import block. The tagged unit is byte-identical (gate-verified) and no helper it calls changed. Verdict stands. Judge rejudge 2026-09-30 (bfd AdminDown, OSPF client). D-8 fixed: engine.runBFDSubscriber (internal/plugins/ospf/bfd_client.go, shared by OSPFv2 and v3) no longer declares the neighbor down on StateAdminDown or on a Down with RemoteAdminDown; the 4.2 quote sits above the statement. + TestOSPFBFDAdminDownTakesNoAction and + TestOSPFBFDRemoteAdminDownTakesNoAction (Up, change, Up; later Up read, neighbor not down, no release, session_down_total 0; arm 2 carries an in-body control: the same Down without the flag still declares the neighbor down). TestOSPFBFDAdminDownTreatedAsDown, which asserted the defect and carried no tag, replaced (D-15). Judge overlays: the old condition reds both new tests; removing only the RemoteAdminDown guard reds only arm 2. BGP arms and engine +/- unchanged (see previous verdict). Every client with independent liveness (BGP hold timer, OSPF RouterDeadInterval) now meets the SHOULD; static routes have none, so treating AdminDown as Down is correct under Section 3.2. Records: revert ospf runBFDSubscriber observed red for both units.

RFC5882-4.2.2.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor). SHIFTED by 6e063fb498 (tests: give ten assert-nothing tests a real assertion), whose hunks sit in untagged sibling tests and the import block. The tagged unit is byte-identical (gate-verified) and no helper it calls changed. Verdict stands. Judge rejudge 2026-09-30 (last five). + reactor TestBFDClient_TeardownOnDown: a non-initial BFD Down StateChange (DiagControlDetectExpired) on an Established peer puts Cease / BFD Down on the wire and moves the session to Idle; asserts the wire, not the opQueue. Producer Peer.runBFDSubscriber -> Session.bfdTeardown (Established arm). MP-BGP is the multi-data-protocol client; ending the session considers the path failed for every family, which is the shared-topology action. {single-polarity: positive} accepted: the obligation is to act on Up->Down and its violation is inaction, which no input presents for refusal; the only no-action boundaries are Up->AdminDown / remote AdminDown (RFC5882-4.2-1, enforced on its own tags, a neighbour row) and the Initial snapshot (not a transition), neither violates this row; no negative existed at HEAD. Record: bfdTeardown revert observed red; author's targeted overlay (Established arm off) red.

RFC5882-4.2.2.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor). SHIFTED by 6e063fb498 (tests: give ten assert-nothing tests a real assertion), whose hunks sit in untagged sibling tests and the import block. The tagged unit is byte-identical (gate-verified) and no helper it calls changed. Verdict stands. Judge rejudge 2026-09-30 (last five). + TestBFDClient_TeardownOnDown: BGP has no per-path announcement short of the session, so Ze emulates the hold-timer outcome: NOTIFICATION then Idle, with RFC 9384 Cease subcode 10 as the code (msg[19]/msg[20] asserted, state polled to Idle). {single-polarity: positive} accepted: action-on-event SHOULD, failure is inaction, no refusal path; the AdminDown no-action case is RFC5882-4.2-1's. Record: bfdTeardown revert observed red.

RFC5882-4.2.2.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor). SHIFTED by 6e063fb498 (tests: give ten assert-nothing tests a real assertion), whose hunks sit in untagged sibling tests and the import block. The tagged unit is byte-identical (gate-verified) and no helper it calls changed. Verdict stands. Judge rejudge 2026-09-30 (last five). Earlier weak note said Ze acts on the whole session rather than one topology. Re-read §4.2.2.2: the SHOULD is 'action SHOULD be taken in the control protocol to signal the lack of connectivity for the path in the topology over which BFD is running'; the next sentence 'Generally, this can be done without impacting the connectivity of other topologies' carries no keyword and states feasibility, not an obligation to spare the others; §10.2 asks the EBGP session 'should be torn down in accordance with Section 3.2'. Ending the BGP session signals the loss in the BFD topology, so the author's reading holds. + TestBFDClient_TeardownOnDown (Cease/BFD Down on the wire, Idle). {single-polarity: positive} accepted for the same reason as 4.2.2.1-1. Record: bfdTeardown revert observed red.

RFC5882-4.4-1.note: Re-judge 2026-10-12 (independent auditor, not the author of the {partial} marker) after the marker was added. RFC 5882 Section 4.4 re-read in rfc/full/rfc5882.txt: 'If multiple control protocols wish to establish BFD sessions with the same remote system for the same data protocol, all MUST share a single BFD session.' Verdict partial. Tested selector: "all MUST share a single BFD session". Gap selector: "with the same remote system". Producer: internal/component/bfd/engine/shared_session.go::sharedEntryLocked (with sharesSession, which it calls). What the tagged bodies check, each with a current verified revert record: TestBFDSharedSessionSameKey (one key, two EnsureSession calls: exactly 1 session at refcount 2, refcount 1 after one release, 0 sessions after the last); TestBFDDistinctSessionsDifferentKey (negative: two peers, 2 sessions each at refcount 1); TestCanonicalCollapsesEveryClientShapeOntoOneKey, TestCanonicalCollapsesMultiHopShapesOntoOneKey, TestPinnedSessionReachesTheSharedKey, TestStrictPeerRequestReachesTheSharedKey, TestOSPFNeighborRequestReachesTheSharedKey (the pinned parser, bfdRequestFor and bfdRequestForNeighbor reach one exact key, asserted by equality, so they share through the exact-key registry); TestMultiHopClientsInAVRFShareOneSession (pinned multi-hop entry with a local address in VRF red, then a BGP request with none through pluginService.EnsureSession: 1 session at refcount 2); TestMultiHopClientsToTwoRemoteSystemsGetTwoSessions (negative: a different peer that matches on every other field gets its own session); TestSharedSessionWidensOnRelease (after a pinned client joins and leaves, entry.joined is the unpinned key again and a client pinned elsewhere gets the same session, 1 session at refcount 2; with the pinned client still attached the other pinned client gets its own, RFC 5883 Section 4.1). Q1 the assertions are session counts and refcounts, which is what the RFC says, not what the code does. Q2 every unit has an observed-red revert record (./le rfc discriminate stem rfc5882: none stale, none unproven). Q3 the engine tests use bare loops and Snapshot, nothing else can cut the count. Q4 not the whole MUST: the two configurations the Gap names still give two sessions by design, read at the producer: sharesSession requires equal interfaces for an IPv6 link-local peer, and sharedEntryLocked answers no session when a request with an unset field matches two or more live sessions (sharedMatch.only). Marker corrected in this re-judge: the earlier Tested reason said the join holds 'in either arrival order' and for 'a request that left a field unset' in general; the tagged bodies check only the multi-hop local-address case, pinned entry first, and no tagged unit drives a single-hop request with an unset interface or local address through sharedEntryLocked, so the reason now names exactly the shapes the bodies check. Not covered by the Gap and not judged here: two clients asking for different hop modes to one peer address get two sessions (sharesSession compares Mode); under the partial rules that obligation stays unproven, not met.
